answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit that is slashed when peers expose fake identities, with reputation earned only through verified work over time. Like a falcon that must prove its hunting skill before joining the flock, an agent's history acts as a prism: it refracts one identity into many checkable signals — completed tasks, peer attestations, and consistent behaviour — so a cheap copy cannot mimic the full spectrum. A quill's signature, a unique cryptographic proof tied to real work, makes mass forgery expensive.
